environmental.intro: All figures are estimates. CO₂ and water are derived from a published benchmark of LLM inference energy, weighted by token type and scaled per model; analogies use average reference values. Treat these as order-of-magnitude indicators, not precise measurements.
environmental.methodology.heading: Calculation & Estimates
environmental.methodology.cost: Cost (UBB) uses GitHub Copilot AI Credit rates (1 credit = $0.01) under Usage Based Billing.
environmental.methodology.co2Paper: CO₂: Jegham et al. estimate 5.671 Wh for one Claude 3.7 Sonnet request with 10,000 input and 1,500 output tokens; at 0.287 kg CO₂e/kWh (AWS) that is about 1.63 g CO₂e. Counting an input token as 1/20 of an output token, that request is 2,000 output-equivalent tokens, giving ~814 g (range 770–857 g) per 1M output-equivalent tokens, rounded up to 840 g.
environmental.methodology.co2Weights: Token weights (output = 1.0, uncached input = 0.05, cache write = 0.0625, cache read = 0.0005) are approximations adopted from neuland/tokendashboard-backend, not values from the paper. The paper does not model prompt caching, and the cache-read weight in particular is a rough guess. Tokens without a per-model breakdown are counted with the reference request's input/output mix.
environmental.methodology.modelScaling: Other models are scaled from the Claude Sonnet baseline by the ratio of their output-token price (for example Haiku ⅓×, Opus 1⅔×). Price stands in for model size here; it is not a measurement. Models without a known price use the Sonnet baseline.
environmental.methodology.water: Water uses the paper's formula: on-site cooling (energy ÷ PUE × 0.18 L/kWh) plus off-site electricity generation (energy × 5.11 L/kWh), with AWS's PUE of 1.14. That is about 30 mL for the reference request, or ~15 L per 1M output-equivalent tokens for Claude Sonnet, scaled per model like CO₂.
environmental.methodology.tree: Tree equivalent represents the fraction of a single mature tree's annual CO₂ absorption (~21 kg/year).
environmental.methodology.co2Analogies: CO₂ analogies: petrol car ≈ 120 g/km · intercity train ≈ 41 g/km · economy flight ≈ 180 g/km (ICAO avg.) · smartphone charge ≈ 8 g · LED bulb ≈ 3 g/hr (10 W, EU grid) · kettle boil ≈ 20 g.
environmental.methodology.waterAnalogies: Water analogies: shower ≈ 8 L/min · washing machine ≈ 50 L · standard bathtub ≈ 150 L · dishwasher ≈ 12 L · mug of tea ≈ 250 mL · daily drinking water ≈ 2 L/person.
environmental.methodology.caveat: All analogies are order-of-magnitude estimates. Actual values depend on your region's energy mix, hardware, model implementation, and caching behavior.
environmental.methodology.paperLink: Jegham et al., "How Hungry is AI?" (arXiv:2505.09598)

usage.claudeDesktopCoverage.tooltip:
Claude Desktop lists every session it knows about, but this extension can only measure sessions whose transcript is still on this machine. Two things remove a transcript from local disk:

• Claude Code deletes transcripts older than its retention window (the cleanupPeriodDays setting, 30 days by default). Raise it in ~/.claude/settings.json to keep more history measurable.
• Sessions that ran in the cloud never write a transcript to this machine at all.

These sessions are not missing from your account — they are just not measurable locally.

insight.shortScatteredSessions.title: ⚡ Consolidate short sessions for deeper focus
insight.shortScatteredSessions.body: You had {0} short sessions today (avg {1} interactions each). Fewer, deeper sessions often produce better results — try keeping context within one session.
insight.marathonSessionToday.title: 🧵 A very long chat session today
insight.marathonSessionToday.body: Your longest chat today{0} reached {1}{2}. Deep work in one chat is great — but once a session gets this long, earlier context is more likely to be summarized, compressed, or dropped, so replies can drift and slow down. When the goal changes, start a fresh chat (New Chat / `/new`) and paste a short handoff summary. A handy rule: one chat per bug, feature, or refactor.
insight.veryLongSessionsPattern.title: 📏 Your chats tend to run long
insight.veryLongSessionsPattern.body: Over the last 30 days your longest conversation reached {0} prompts, and your sessions average {1} prompts each. Very long chats make earlier context less reliable — the assistant may compress or ignore it as the window fills. Keeping one focused chat per task (and starting fresh when the topic shifts) usually produces sharper, faster answers.
insight.frequentManualCompaction.title: 🎉 You're managing context like a pro
insight.frequentManualCompaction.body: You've used `/compact` {0} times in the last 30 days — that shows deliberate context management, which is a real power-user habit. One refinement: `/compact` is best for continuing the *same task* when a chat gets long. When you're switching to a *new subtask*, a fresh chat (`/new`) with a short handoff summary usually produces sharper answers, since compaction already condenses earlier detail. Rule of thumb: `/compact` = same task, `/new` = new goal.
insight.autoCompactionPattern.title: ⚠️ Your sessions are auto-compacting frequently
insight.autoCompactionPattern.body.one: Your sessions automatically compacted {0} time in the last 7 days ({1}).{2} Auto-compaction means earlier context was lost without your control — you may have noticed replies suddenly lacking earlier detail. To avoid this: start a fresh chat (`/new`) when switching tasks, and use `/compact` yourself in Claude before the window fills.
insight.autoCompactionPattern.body.other: Your sessions automatically compacted {0} times in the last 7 days ({1}).{2} Auto-compaction means earlier context was lost without your control — you may have noticed replies suddenly lacking earlier detail. insight.contextWindowNearLimit.body: {0} of your {1} sessions with measured context fill reached at least {2}% of their context window in the last 30 days.{3}{4} Once a window fills, the client silently drops or summarizes earlier turns — answers start losing detail you already gave. Head it off by starting a fresh chat (`/new`) per task with a short handoff summary, running `/compact` yourself while you still control what's kept, and narrowing context to the files that matter instead of whole-repo references.

insight.contextWindowHealthy.body: None of your {0} sessions with measured context fill came close to their context window in the last 30 days{1}. That means no silent compaction and no lost earlier detail, which is exactly where you want to be. Keep scoping one task per chat and pointing at specific files rather than the whole repo.

Reserve the heavier models for complex multi-step reasoning, architecture decisions, or subtle bugs.

insight.reasoningEffortSwitcher.title: 🎯 You're tuning reasoning effort — nice!
insight.reasoningEffortSwitcher.body: You switched reasoning effort {0} times across {1} sessions. Adapting effort to task complexity is one of the clearest signs of AI-engineering fluency — you're getting more out of Copilot without wasting compute on simple asks.

insight.subagentDelegation.title: 🧩 You're delegating work to sub-agents!

insight.singleFileEditsOnly.body: You've made {0} edit-mode sessions over the last 30 days, all touching a single file. whatsNew.release.0.19.1.headline: The Tools & Integrations tab now shows how reliable and how slow each tool is, which MCP servers fail, and a cost-vs-speed map of your built-in, subagent and skill tools.
whatsNew.feature.usage.tool-execution-st: Tool reliability, latency and MCP health

Four new sections on the Tools & Integrations tab, built from the per-call outcomes your session logs already record: success vs. failure per tool, p50/p95 observed duration per tool, calls and error share per MCP server, and a cost-vs-speed map of built-in, subagent and skill tools (latency × tokens per call, bubble size = calls). Recorded from Copilot CLI, JetBrains, Claude Code and Claude Desktop sessions.
whatsNew.feature.whatsnew.view-index.des: A searchable map of every view, tab and section in the extension, on its own tab here in What's New. Search by name or by what it shows, then jump straight to that tab and section.
whatsNew.tabs.label: What's New sections
whatsNew.footer: Running version {0}. The full changelog, including fixes, ships with the extension.
viewIndex.intro: Every view you can open, with its tabs and sections. Session logs open from Recent Sessions. Search by name, by what it shows, or by a word you remember — the search is forgiving about typos and word order. Use the open button on a line to go straight there.
viewIndex.noMatchStatus: Nothing matches “{0}”. Try fewer or shorter words.
viewIndex.noMatch: No matching views, tabs or sections.
whatsNew.logviewerHint: Open a session from this list to see it in the Session Log Viewer.
whatsNew.release.0.19.0.headline: Usage Analysis is now organized into Usage, Workspace, GitHub and Coaching groups, with banded sections, official editor logos in the Chart view and Copilot budget for every signed-in GitHub account.
whatsNew.release.0.18.3.headline: A maintenance release: the AI Readiness tab now collapses each repository to one row and can draft a Copilot Chat prompt for the controls you pick, plus friendlier MCP tool names. No new screens.
whatsNew.release.0.18.2.headline: See which repository controls are in place, and which still need evidence, in the new AI Readiness tab.
whatsNew.release.0.18.1.headline: A maintenance release: friendly tool names, localization groundwork, and a Mistral Vibe cost-attribution fix. No new screens.
whatsNew.feature.usage.group-tabs.title: Grouped tabs
whatsNew.feature.usage.group-tabs.descri: The ten Usage Analysis tabs now sit under four group tabs (Usage, Workspace, GitHub, Coaching), and My Activity is split into Overview, Spend & models and Context bands.
whatsNew.feature.usage.readiness-tab.des: In Usage Analysis, scan each repository's delivery and governance controls to see what blocks its next stage and what could not be checked. Separate from your personal Fluency Score.
whatsNew.release.0.18.0.headline: This release is about noticing patterns you would otherwise have to spot yourself: what a model router did off screen, where the agent had to backtrack, which prompts you keep retyping, how quickly models actually start answering, and how much Copilot agent memory has piled up on disk.
usage.toolExec.reliability.title: Tool execution reliability
usage.toolExec.reliability.subtitle: Successful and failed calls per tool, last 30 days, counting only calls whose session log recorded an outcome (Copilot CLI, JetBrains, Claude Code, Claude Desktop). Starts without a result are not counted either way.
usage.toolExec.latency.title: Tool latency profile
usage.toolExec.latency.subtitle: Observed execution duration by tool, last 30 days: the time from a tool call starting to its result arriving, so permission prompts and queueing are included. Bar = p50, marker = p95.
usage.toolExec.mcp.title: MCP server health
usage.toolExec.mcp.subtitle: Calls with a recorded outcome and the share that failed, by connected MCP server, last 30 days.
usage.toolExec.costSpeed.title: Cost vs speed map
usage.toolExec.costSpeed.subtitle: p50 latency × result tokens per completed call for each built-in, subagent or skill tool, last 30 days. Bubble size is the number of completed calls; colour is the tool kind. MCP calls are tracked per server in MCP server health and are not plotted here.
usage.toolExec.empty.reliability: No tool outcome data yet. Copilot CLI, JetBrains, Claude Code and Claude Desktop sessions record whether each tool call succeeded; refresh after new sessions.
usage.toolExec.empty.latency: No tool latency data yet. It is recorded from Copilot CLI, JetBrains, Claude Code and Claude Desktop sessions.
usage.toolExec.empty.mcp: No MCP server calls with a recorded outcome in this period.
usage.toolExec.empty.costSpeed: No tools have both latency and output-token data yet.
whatsNew.feature.usage.memory-files-hygi: A new section on the Tools tab showing how much Copilot agent memory has accumulated on disk — per workspace, repo, session, and global scope — with counts for stale and oversized files so you know what is safe to clear out.
whatsNew.feature.logviewer.hydrafusion-r: When a Copilot CLI session runs on HydraFusion, several models draft, judge and repair one answer behind the scenes and you are shown one result and one credit number. This section opens that up: which models ran, who rejected whom, which leg you actually read, and what share of the credits went on review rather than on the answer.
whatsNew.feature.usage.corrections-tab.d: Shows the moments where things went sideways — a tool call that failed, an edit the agent immediately redid, a "sorry, let me try that again" — grouped per repository. A good place to look when a session felt like hard work but you cannot say why.
whatsNew.feature.usage.skill-suggestions: Clusters the opening prompt of your recent sessions to find the task you keep asking for by hand. Each cluster is a candidate for a reusable skill, prompt file, or custom agent.
whatsNew.feature.diagnostics.ttft-tab.de: How long each model takes to start answering you, averaged by day, week, and month with a trendline. Read straight from Copilot Chat's own debug log, so there is nothing to switch on.
whatsNew.feature.whatsnew.view.title: What's New view
whatsNew.feature.whatsnew.view.descripti: The last few releases in plain English, with a way in to each new view, tab, and section from here. Also where the extension sends you when it points something out.
whatsNew.release.0.17.2.headline: A maintenance release: cold-boot token counts, worktree detection, and the Recent Sessions list all stopped getting things wrong. No new screens.
whatsNew.release.0.17.1.headline: Two fixes for stats that under-reported: the Efficiency view no longer gets stuck after you close and reopen it, and sessions spanning midnight now count toward today.
whatsNew.release.0.17.0.headline: The release that made the data comparative: efficiency over time, and per-model numbers you can rank against each other rather than read one at a time.
whatsNew.feature.efficiency.view.title: Efficiency view
whatsNew.feature.efficiency.view.descrip: Answers one question over the long run: are you getting more done per token than you were a month ago? Trends rather than totals.
Per-model one-shot edit rate, retry rate, cost per turn and cache hit rate in one sortable table — so "which model should I use for this" stops being a guess.
whatsNew.feature.chart.cost-by-model-spl: Cost by Model and Tokens by Provider
The usage chart can now be split by model or by provider, and the By Editor breakdown collapses out of the way when you are not reading it.
whatsNew.release.0.13.0.headline: Long-context pricing became visible: the extension now knows when a request crossed into long-context rates and what that cost you.
whatsNew.feature.usage.context-window.de: How full your context windows run, and which requests tipped into long-context pricing. Large contexts are billed differently, and this is where that shows up.
